stories.headline: Iran prepares terms to reopen Strait of Hormuz during US conflict
stories.body:
Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei announced that Iran is drawing up conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz [c9]. Mediators asked Tehran to set out its terms [c9]. Rezaei serves as secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council [c5]. He said Iran exported 80 million barrels of oil during a ceasefire period [c8].

Under a June memorandum of understanding, Iran agreed to clear mines [c10]. Iran also agreed to permit free vessel passage in the Strait of Hormuz for 60 days [c10]. In return, the United States agreed to lift its blockade [c10]. The US also agreed to ease sanctions [c10].

US President Donald Trump rejected re-establishing the terms of that June agreement [c3]. Oil prices rose after reports of his decision [c3]. Trump declared in the Oval Office that US forces had cleared mines from the Strait of Hormuz [c11]. He said that the waterway was open [c11]. Trump later told Al Jazeera that he has no time schedule for negotiations with Iran [c12]. He said he is in no hurry to resume talks [c12].

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions named Operation Economic Outcast [c4]. The sanctions target nearly 60 Iran-linked individuals, entities, and vessels [c4]. The measures aim to pressure Iran during the war with the US [c4]. Rezaei warned that Iran will target US economic interests 100 percent if the US blockade continues [c5]. He said Iran will act with intensity and force [c5].

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Iran has the legitimate right to target the origin of any act of aggression [c6]. He pointed specifically to US refueling aircraft departing from Bulgaria [c6]. Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran [c7]. They met to discuss regional security and conditions for dialogue [c7].

The conflict has affected military readiness elsewhere. US defense and NATO officials said the US military faces a critical shortage of Patriot missile interceptors in Europe [c13]. The shortage happened because interceptor stocks were redeployed to the Middle East for the war with Iran [c13]. The Wall Street Journal reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow [c14]. He went to warn Russia not to attack NATO countries [c14].

In Australia, environmental authorities face avian health issues. A common dolphin found near Goolwa in South Australia tested positive for H5 bird flu [c2]. It is the second native mammal species in Australia confirmed with the virus [c2]. The Australian government decided to withdraw 24 expeditioners from its Macquarie Island research station [c1]. The government took action because of psychosocial risks from an expected H5 avian influenza mortality event [c1].

vocab.meaning: members of an exploratory or scientific group
a defensive weapon meant to destroy incoming missiles
the blocking of access or transport to a country or region

stories.headline: Trump orders federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America [c15]. Lake Ontario lies along the border separating New York from the Canadian province of Ontario [c24]. The name originates from the Huron Indigenous word oniatari:io, meaning lake of shining waters [c23].

The US Geological Survey updated the name in its Geographic Names Information System [c16]. Democratic Representative Debbie Dingell of Michigan announced plans to introduce legislation in Congress to nullify the order [c20].

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on social media that Canadians know things must be called by their name [c19]. Carney said the lake is called Lake Ontario today and forever [c19].

Trump previously issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America [c18]. That order led to a legal dispute with Mexico and a lawsuit by the Associated Press [c18]. Trump also posted an altered 1948 Life magazine graphic on social media [c17]. The graphic placed him at the top under a new category named greatest [c17].

Trade tensions between the countries remain high. The US put 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods [c22]. The tariffs were imposed after trade negotiations collapsed between Washington and Ottawa [c22]. Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said on X that the US withdrew demands on French language labeling [c21].

vocab.meaning: taxes imposed by a government on imported goods

stories.headline: Meta agrees to multi-billion settlements over youth safety claims
stories.body:
Tech company Meta agreed to pay major financial settlements to resolve state and federal child safety lawsuits in the United States [c26, c30]. One report stated Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit from 29 US states [c26]. Another report put the 29-state settlement figure at $16.68 billion [c27].

Meta also reached a broader deal covering 47 states and territories for up to $17.1 billion in penalties [c33]. That deal includes a separate $1 billion settlement in Texas [c33]. Meta agreed to pay up to $17 billion to settle a federal lawsuit brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey [c30]. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers approved the multi-state agreement in federal court in Oakland, California [c34].

As part of the settlement, Meta agreed to implement a default two-hour daily time limit for users under 18 [c31]. Meta will also set a default block on nighttime use [c31]. It will ban displaying like and reaction counts [c31].

British minister Pat McFadden said the UK does not want American children receiving higher protection than British children [c35].

In 2025, Meta generated $198.8 billion in revenue and $102.5 billion in operating profit [c28].

vocab.meaning: punishments or financial fines imposed for breaking laws
an official agreement that resolves a legal dispute

stories.headline: Glacial collapse triggers fatal flood in Nepal and Tibet region
stories.body:
A massive glacial collapse triggered sudden flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border, killing hundreds of people and leaving many missing [c38, c50]. The US Geological Survey clarified that a collapsed glacier caused the disaster [c50]. The impact of the falling glacier hitting the valley floor registered a seismic magnitude of 5.2 [c51].

An analysis by ICIMOD found that an ice-rock avalanche entered the Lende Khola tributary [c52]. The flood caused downstream river levels to rise by 7 to 9 metres within 30 minutes [c52]. The disaster occurred in Nepal's northern Rasuwa district without earlier rainfall in the immediate area to warn residents [c54]. Flooding struck along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river systems [c36].

Nepal Police reported that 469 people died as of Friday [c38]. Police reported that 1,545 people were rescued or injured [c38]. Authorities deployed 4,348 police personnel for search and rescue operations across affected districts [c39]. Nepali army helicopter rescue teams worked to rescue about 100 people trapped inside a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project [c42].

Hundreds of foreign citizens remain missing in Nepal. Nepal Police reported that missing foreigners include 178 Indians, 65 Americans, 51 Malaysians, 53 Ukrainians, 33 Britons, 35 Australians, and 25 Canadians [c40]. India's Ministry of External Affairs said that 290 Indians in Nepal remain unaccounted for [c53]. The ministry added that about 200 Indians stranded on the Chinese side after the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra sought assistance [c53].

Across the border in Tibet, Chinese state media reported that at least 558 people were missing [c44]. That number includes at least 260 foreign nationals [c44]. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that 555 stranded tourists and 499 local residents were transported out of the disaster zone in Tibet by Friday morning [c43].

Individual families are searching for news of loved ones. Rakesh Nayak, a 45-year-old software engineer from Karnataka living in Australia, went missing near the border during an Isha Foundation tour [c47]. He was last known to be inside an immigration office at about 9:10 pm on August 26 [c48]. Flash floods struck twenty minutes later [c48]. At least 13 people from Karnataka are stranded in Nepal and Tibet [c49].

Nepal declined search and rescue team deployment offers from foreign countries [c36]. Offers came from India, China, the US, UK, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh [c37]. The United States pledged $500,000, and the World Health Organization sent emergency medical supplies [c41]. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher released $2 million in emergency funds [c46]. The Red Cross launched an emergency appeal for $31 million to help an estimated 93,000 affected people [c45].

vocab.meaning: a river or stream flowing into a larger river or lake
relating to earthquakes or vibrations of the earth
a large mass of ice, snow, or rock falling down a mountain

stories.headline: Indian tribunal approves 99.97% debt haircut for Subhash Chandra
stories.body:
The National Company Law Tribunal approved a personal insolvency plan for Essel Group chairman Subhash Chandra [c55]. The ruling allows Chandra to pay Rs 6.5 crore against creditor claims of over Rs 22,000 crore [c55]. Under the plan, creditors will recover about 0.028% of their claims, or three paise for every Rs 100 owed [c66]. For example, LIC Housing Finance had an admitted claim of Rs 1,322.39 crore, but its approved repayment is Rs 38,09,294 [c67].

NCLT Member Nilesh Sharma approved the plan as a third member after a split verdict by a two-member bench [c65]. Creditors holding 80.8% of voting rights approved the plan [c61]. Dissenting lenders representing about 15% argued that related entities like Veena Investments controlled over 61% of votes [c61, c62]. HDFC Bank said it is exploring an appeal against the 99.97% debt haircut [c59].

Political opposition leaders criticized the ruling. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called the tribunal the Neta-Company Loot Tribunal [c56]. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh called the 99.97% debt reduction a mockery of insolvency laws [c57]. Chandra's office said he was only a personal guarantor and had not borrowed money personally [c58]. Chandra served as an Independent MP backed by the BJP from 2016 to 2022 [c69].

vocab.meaning: the state of being unable to pay debts owed
a person who promises to pay a debt if the borrower fails to pay

stories.headline: Narendra Modi plans visit to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan for summit
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will begin a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic on August 29 [c70]. Modi will visit Uzbekistan from August 29 to 30 before traveling to the Kyrgyz Republic from August 31 to September 1 [c70].

In Tashkent, Modi will hold talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to strengthen their strategic partnership [c71]. Bilateral trade and investment between India and Uzbekistan stand close to $1 billion [c72]. More than 16,000 Indian students study in Uzbekistan, which hosts four Indian university campuses [c73]. Modi will also visit the Lal Bahadur Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre [c74].

Modi will then attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek [c75, c80]. The summit marks the 25th anniversary of the organization, which India joined in 2017 [c80]. On the sidelines, Modi will hold a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin [c75]. Ahead of the summit, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Putin in Moscow [c76]. Putin assured Jaishankar that Russia will continue supplying fertilizers to Indian farmers [c78].

Modi is also scheduled to host Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in India for a BRICS summit on September 12 and 13 [c79].

vocab.meaning: a planned route or travel schedule
